models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Benign, light-air pattern over the Aeolians right now - 1-6 kt and flat seas - but the trip dates are still too far out to bank on.
briefing.synopsis: Current consensus across the available models shows a slack gradient over the islands: winds generally 1-6 kt with no settled direction, swinging between NE in the small hours, N to NW in the afternoons and a southerly component at Portorosa. Seas are essentially flat - 0.1-0.4 ft total wave and swell at every island through 03 Oct. Gusts are the only variation worth noting, to 15.6 kt at Stromboli at 18:00 on 01 Oct (ECMWF IFS 0.25°, 30 Sep 18Z), and IFS gusts are interval maxima so they look large against a 6 kt mean. Where the models do split in the short term they split hard on strength: 0.5-8.0 kt at Portorosa and 3.3-9.8 kt at Panarea for 06:00 on 01 Oct - that is a genuine spread, not a mean to be trusted.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: The pre-departure berth on the night of 03 Oct is Portorosa Marina, and it is the only option listed - an enclosed marina with all-round shelter, so the choice does not matter. Guidance for that night is 3.7 kt SE, gusting 8.4 kt, with 0.1 ft NNW swell. Nothing in the payload suggests any reason to move; the practical caveat is simply that 03 Oct is still two days out and the detail will change.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Tomorrow is a shore day - the fleet departs in two days. For the first leg, Portorosa to Lipari on 04 Oct, the current guidance gives a 06:00 departure in 5.4 kt SSE, gusting 11.9 kt, 0.1 ft sea, a 22 nm run on 342 degrees true, arriving about 09:00. Treat that window as a placeholder: re-brief on the morning of departure, when ICON-2i (2 km) will actually cover the leg.

passage_notes.note: 22 nm, 342T. Early guidance: 5.4 kt SSE at 06:00, 0.1 ft sea - a run, likely motoring. Verdict 'go' but at 3-day lead.
12 nm, 029T. 2-4 kt ENE to NNE, 0.1 ft sea. Looks like a motor if it verifies.
26 nm, 034T. 2-4 kt N to NE, 0.1 ft sea. Light and largely on the nose in current guidance.
11 nm, 219T. 4-5 kt, backing SW through the morning, 0.3-0.5 ft sea.
28 nm, 259T. The breeziest leg shown: 6.5-7.1 kt SW, gusts to 13.8 kt, 0.7-0.9 ft - close hauled. At the very edge of the forecast horizon (07 Oct 23:00).
No forecast - beyond the model horizon. Only a rehearsal run against earlier live weather exists; it is not a forecast for your date.

cautions: Everything from 04 Oct on is at 3-6 days lead. Forecast stability over 72-120 h shows mean direction shifts of 67 degrees - speeds are stable but direction is not, so plan points of sail loosely.
ICON-2i (01 Oct 00Z) only runs ~60-72 h ahead, so none of the trip days are covered by the 2 km grid yet; the trip-date numbers rest on ECMWF IFS and AIFS (both 30 Sep 18Z) alone.

Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli is open from every direction and anchoring is not permitted - it only works while it stays calm, as it currently does (3.8 kt NE, 0.2 ft swell). Any build-up and the Stromboli option should be dropped.
Gust figures from IFS are interval maxima, so ratios like 10 kt gusts over a 4 kt mean are a model artefact in light air rather than a squall signal.
The 06:00 model spread of 0.5-8.0 kt at Portorosa and 2.1-8.7 kt at Lipari shows how little the models agree on strength even at short range in this slack pattern.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS and AIFS agree that the pattern is slack and the seas flat, and run-to-run wind shifts have averaged only 0.7 kt out to 120 h, but direction is swinging by tens of degrees between runs and the fine-grid model does not yet reach the trip dates.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
